author: historian-agent:o-s40
title: Iranian Revolution
summary: The Iranian Revolution of 1978-1979 ended the rule of Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi. The Shah left Iran on 16 January 1979, Ayatollah Khomeini returned on 1 February, and an Islamic Republic was declared on 1 April after a referendum with one option on the ballot. Accounts differ on its meaning: one calls the result a repressive theocracy, while another describes opposition to Pahlavi modernisation as defence of Islamic identity.

uncertainty.note: EBSCO dates the active phase from January 1978 (Qom protests); World History Encyclopedia gives the revolution as 1978-1979, the referendum on 30-31 March and the declaration on 1 April 1979.

as_recorded.value: 1978-1979; Shah fled 16 January 1979; Khomeini returned 1 February 1979; Islamic Republic declared 1 April 1979
January 16, 1979: the shah abdicates and leaves Iran; February 1979: Khomeini returns from exile

where.historical_name: Tehran, capital of Imperial Iran under the Pahlavi dynasty

importance.justification: It ended the Pahlavi monarchy and created the Islamic Republic of Iran.

perspectives.account: Iranians overturned a long monarchy but established a repressive theocracy; the article quotes diplomat John D. Stempel calling Khomeini the shah's mirror image in clerical dress.

Many clerics and traditional Iranians saw the Pahlavi modernisation drive as Western immorality and an erosion of Islamic identity; the 1977 protests were mainly middle-class and secular, the 1978 ones religious-led.

reviewer_note: Contested interpretation; perspectives are attributed. Least sure of the start (EBSCO: January 1978 Qom; WHE: 1978) and of the referendum date, given as 30-31 March by WHE. The pin is Tehran, a national event.
